claims.statement: GatewayHandler shares serving dependencies while routing session state, DML buffers, prepared statements, portals, and cached results by connection ID.
Simple queries resolve a stable connection ID, reject draining requests, handle empty input, and sequentially dispatch parseable multi-statement SQL through do_query_single.

Extended Parse/Bind/Execute uses prepared statements and portals, while custom Execute collects complete query results before implementing max_rows delivery and PortalSuspended through cached offsets.
Malformed supported binary Bind values return 22P03 and invalid parameter counts or format codes return 08P01 before execution, discard messages until Sync, and preserve the connection.
Authentication-off startup assigns the System principal; session state owns the authenticated principal, namespace, transaction state, freshness settings, and cancellation identity.

Mutation dispatch checks policy-required ACL roles for non-System principals and audits denial; the shared read guard checks Viewer access and cross-namespace catalog-view access, and query-time execution checks all referenced relations.
SUBSCRIBE authorizes before exposing retention metadata, scanning snapshots, or acquiring a stream slot, and COPY OUT checks read access before reading or emitting COPY frames.

INSERT stages stored row values and deterministic keys with primary-key checks; UPDATE stages old/new row images and keys; DELETE captures pre-images before appending mutations to the connection write buffer.
INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE autocommit through handle_commit outside an explicit transaction, while explicit blocks retain buffered operations until COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

A multi-row UPDATE expression failure can occur before candidate mutations enter the buffer; the regression test verifies division-by-zero leaves both base table and materialized view unchanged, but per-operation buffer pushes do not provide an atomic whole-statement capacity reservation.

WriteBuffer accounts approximate operation bytes with a default 64 MiB bound and rejects overflowing pushes; savepoints are bounded to 128 and rollback-to truncates buffered operations to a recorded position.

Read Committed is the supported session isolation; Serializable and Repeatable Read are rejected, and two-phase transaction commands are unsupported rather than providing a transaction-wide snapshot guarantee.

ROLLBACK clears buffered DML and pending transactional notifications without shard writes; successful explicit transaction completion clears cursors and local settings, and failed blocks allow rollback forms while rejecting other commands including SUBSCRIBE with 25P02.

Commit checks explicit idempotency keys for prior epochs and persists dedup metadata with table mutations; absent a supplied envelope it generates a new key per commit rather than a stable identity for independent client retries.

Local commit drains mutations, holds shard_commit_lock across normalization, epoch allocation, table/frontier write, dependent view refresh, flush, and subscription publication, then releases it before recording session freshness and returning completion.
ShardDb writes a table batch as one SlateDB batch and awaits durability, but updates its in-memory last_epoch from a frontier entry before the underlying write finishes.

Compiled-view refresh processes deltas, writes sink output, then persists pipeline state; local commit logs refresh failures as warnings while distributed source-delta submission failures propagate, so table writes and all dependent-view work are not one atomic batch.

Subscription changes are published per table only after storage flush while holding the commit lock; UPDATE publishes a negative old row and positive new row at one epoch, and replay overflow after persistence requires resnapshot without rolling back the durable transaction.
Commit failures after the table write do not imply no state persisted; without a configured shard, handle_commit instead discards buffered writes and returns a best-effort completion.
Local serving reads prefer ShardDb, resolve compiled sink output by catalog operator ID, and otherwise scan legacy prefixes; ordinary read_view_response does not acquire the local commit mutex.

Read-only serving uses the injected ViewReader; HotOnlyViewReader resolves compiled view directory entries and materializes weighted sink output, falls back to legacy prefixes, and carries a frontier label from reader opening; distributed-data-plane view reads instead merge workload snapshots.

SELECT dispatch has distinct index, catalog, serving-view, relation query-time DataFusion, and literal DataFusion branches; relation query-time execution registers streaming tables over selected shard readers and collects SQL result batches.

Query-time topology selection prefers a refresh provider, then configured topology, then a known local shard; provider refresh reopens all readers and rejects unequal persisted frontiers or unavailable topology instead of returning a local partial result.

MultiShardReader is a separate legacy-prefix scatter/union helper whose frontier is supplied by its caller; scatter_read does not itself reopen historical readers or pin storage by epoch and checks merged size after materializing shard results.

Relation reads prioritize explicit AFTER or one-shot wait_for tokens over automatic committed-write freshness; automatic waiting defaults to enabled with a 5000 ms timeout, polls local last_epoch every 10 ms, and logs then proceeds on timeout rather than failing the query.

Local snapshot SUBSCRIBE reserves a drop-owned slot, holds the commit mutex while capturing epoch and bounded snapshot, releases it before streaming, emits snapshot rows before later deltas with mz_timestamp and mz_diff, and polls idle tails every 100 ms; distributed snapshot fencing remains separate.

AS OF EPOCH replay is inclusive and validates retained history; the replay registry is bounded in-memory state, fails closed for unobserved or lost history, and is not durable replay across gateway restart.

Subscription logs enforce whole monotone epochs and whole-epoch eviction; an oversized epoch clears replay and advances its floor, while active subscribers losing their next position fail as too slow instead of silently skipping changes.
Subscriptions have bounds of 16 active streams, 10000 snapshot rows, default 10000 retained entries, 16 MiB retained payload per relation, and 8 MiB per epoch, with drop-owned stream permits.

Query-time scatter tracks cumulative row and byte budgets with in-flight metrics; COPY OUT guards output before frames and imposes a producer-read deadline without claiming complete producer admission.

View capacity admission can pause lower-priority workloads or reject capacity requests, while backfill admission uses an independent reservation lane that does not pause running views; these are separate from ordinary SELECT scheduling.

CancelRequest matches backend PID and secret on a separate connection and signals a token; inspected serving-read and query-time DataFusion branches race that token and return 57014, but handle_commit has no equivalent cancellation race.
Connection teardown removes prepared statements, portal tracking and cached rows, sessions, write buffers, and COPY state, including socket termination paths.

Focused DML tests cover expression failure atomicity, primary-key update propagation, rollback, and atomic commit epochs, while durable-publication regressions cover exact rows, ordered concurrent publication, and local snapshot fencing but explicitly leave process-destruction durability to release qualification.
